'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Tigray War]]
**[[Ethiopian National Defense Force|ENDF]] [[airstrike]]s on the city of [[Mekelle]] in [[Ethiopia]]'s [[Tigray Region]] kill at least three people. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/18/air-strikes-hit-capital-of-ethiopias-tigray-regional-media (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021 Eswatini protests]]
**[[Prime Minister of Eswatini|Prime Minister]] [[Cleopas Dlamini]] orders the closure of schools across [[Eswatini]] in an attempt to stop pro-[[democracy]] protests that have occurred across the kingdom in the past few months. Protesters demand an end to the [[absolute monarchy]] of King [[Mswati III]], the last of its kind in [[Africa]], as ministers back the move, saying that there "is no room for such anarchy in our society". [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-10-18/schools-shut-as-pro-democracy-protests-escalate-in-eswatini (''Bloomberg'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[MeToo movement]]
**German [[publishing house]] [[Axel Springer SE|Axel Springer]] dismisses [[Julian Reichelt]] as the [[editor-in-chief]] of its [[Tabloid journalism|tabloid]] newspaper ''[[Bild]]'' following [[sexual harassment]] complaints against Reichelt from his [[co-worker]]s. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/10/18/business/media/julian-reichelt-axel-springer.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in Africa]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Burundi]]
*****[[Burundi]] launches its [[COVID-19 vaccination in Burundi|COVID-19 vaccination]] rollout using part of a shipment of 500,000 doses of the [[Sinopharm BIBP COVID-19 vaccine]] donated by [[China]] in a shift to make the country more active in its approach to containing the [[pandemic]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/burundi-launches-covid-19-vaccination-drive-2021-10-18/ (Reuters)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe]]
*****[[Zimbabwe]] bans [[COVID-19 vaccination in Zimbabwe|unvaccinated]] [[civil servant]]s from working in an effort to reduce the spread of [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.newsday.co.zw/2021/10/unvaccinated-civil-servants-fired/ (Newsday)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] surpasses eight million cases of COVID-19 after reporting a record for the fourth consecutive day of 34,325 new cases. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/russias-coronavirus-infections-exceed-million-80638769 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[President of the Government of Aragon]] [[Javier Lambán]] tests positive for COVID-19 after attending the [[PSOE]]'s three-day party congress in [[Valencia]]. [https://www.elmundo.es/espana/2021/10/18/616d1df0e4d4d8e63f8b458d.html (''El Mundo'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] reports a record 538 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 61,348. [https://dip.org.ua/en/news-of-the-mfa-of-ukraine/ukraine-broke-the-record-for-mortality-from-covid-19/ (DIP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New South Wales]]
****Restrictions are eased further in [[New South Wales]] as more than 80% of the adult population are now fully vaccinated against COVID-19. Limits on private gatherings and density caps at businesses are relaxed, and schools begin a phased reopening. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/oct/18/nsw-is-opening-up-further-from-monday-what-extra-freedoms-do-people-have-now (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tasmania]]
****The [[COVID-19 lockdown|lockdown]] is lifted across southern [[Tasmania]], including the state capital [[Hobart]]. The lockdown was initiated because a person with COVID-19 entered the state, but was lifted when no community transmission was reported. [https://www.news.com.au/travel/travel-updates/health-safety/tasmania-to-exit-three-day-snap-lockdown-as-planned/news-story/2ba10a42056bf97571a96d607526dba9 (News.com.au)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***The U.S. surpasses 45 million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.kiro7.com/news/trending/coronavirus-total-us-covid-19-cases-top-45-million-death-toll-surpasses-725000/QXGFH26CTFBRPBIRYPY3HUVMBY/ (KIRO-TV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maryland]]
****Former [[United States Secretary of State|U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Colin Powell]] dies from COVID-19 at the age of 84 at [[Walter Reed National Military Medical Center]] in [[Bethesda, Maryland]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/10/18/us/politics/colin-powell-dead.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***Phase three trial results suggest that the [[Valneva COVID-19 vaccine|Valneva COVID vaccine]] is effective at priming the [[immune system]] to fight COVID-19. [https://www.bbc.com/news/health-58952473 (BBC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Russia]] announces that it will be suspending its mission to [[NATO]] in [[Brussels]] as early as November 1, in response to the expulsion of 8 [[diplomat]]s accused of [[espionage]] from the mission earlier this month. The NATO information bureau and military liaison in [[Moscow]] will also be terminated. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/10/18/europe/russia-suspends-nato-mission-intl/index.html (CNN)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2016 Karrada bombing]]
**[[Iraq]] receives Ghazwan al-Zawbaee, the alleged mastermind of the [[Islamic State|ISIL]] [[car bomb|suicide truck bomb]]ing that killed 340 people in [[Karrada]], [[Baghdad]], in 2016, which was the deadliest single-bomb attack in Iraq. Al-Zawbaee was arrested two days prior through a joint operation in a neighboring country. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-58957048 (BBC News)]
*[[2021 Bangladesh communal violence]]
**At least 300 suspected members of a [[Islam|Muslim]] mob are arrested for the killing of two [[Hinduism|Hindu]] men three days ago at a temple in [[Noakhali District|Noakhali]], [[Bangladesh]]. The violence occurred after an alleged [[Quran desecration]] at a [[Hindu temple]] in [[Haziganj Upazila]]. Several Hindu temples were also damaged in the clashes. Four members of the mob were also killed when [[Bangladesh Police]] personnel opened fire in [[Chandpur, Bangladesh|Chandpur]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/18/bangladesh-hindus-men-killed-temples-vandalised-religious-violence (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**[[Chairman of the State Administration Council|State Administration Council chairman]] [[Min Aung Hlaing]] announces that his [[State Administration Council|military junta]] will release a total of 5,636 jailed protesters to commemorate the [[Thadingyut Festival]]. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/overseas/10/18/21/myanmar-to-release-over-5000-anti-coup-protesters (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]
*Three people are killed and three more injured during a [[police raid]] at a compound of a religious group in [[Montego Bay]], [[Jamaica]], due to concerns that they were preparing [[Human sacrifice|ritual killings]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/three-people-dead-after-jamaica-police-raid-cult-compound-fear-ritualized-2021-10-18/ (Reuters)]
*Citing ''[[Roe v. Wade]]'', the [[United States Department of Justice]] requests the [[Supreme Court of the United States|Supreme Court]] to vacate the mandate of the [[United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit|Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit]] on allowing the [[Texas Heartbeat Act]] to remain in effect, thereby blocking the law. [https://today.rtl.lu/news/world/a/1803728.html (AFP via RTL)]
*[[President of Ecuador|Ecuadorian president]] [[Guillermo Lasso]] declares a [[Ecuador|nationwide]] [[state of emergency]], citing an increase in [[drug-related crime]]. [https://mb.com.ph/2021/10/19/ecuador-president-declares-state-of-emergency-over-drug-violence/ (AFP via ''Manila Bulletin'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Egor Babaev]] and collaborators with the [[KTH Royal Institute of Technology]] publish an experiment showing evidence of a new [[state of matter]] called [[electron quadruplets]]. [https://phys.org/news/2021-10-reveal-formation-state-electron-quadruplets.html (Phys.org)]
